texto:
October 27, 1962. Soviet missiles are in Cuba, and Moscow sends a second, tougher letter: take your missiles out of Turkey.

That morning, an American U-2 is shot down over Cuba. The pilot is killed. Moscow never ordered it.

That night, the President's brother meets the Soviet ambassador alone. His memo says there could be no deal.

But one sentence in that memo is crossed out. It says: "per your instructions, I mentioned four or five months."

By April 1963, the missiles in Turkey were gone. Only nine American officials knew why.
